idiom_name: Readonly<Frame> current / mutable next with a destructuring swap
implementation_notes: TypeScript realizes the JavaScript mechanism and adds a compile-time contract: model the published frame as `Readonly<Frame>` (or `readonly` properties) and the back buffer as a separate mutable type, so the type checker rejects writes to the published snapshot - `Readonly<Type>` 'constructs a type with all properties of Type set to readonly'. The swap stays a single assignment, which is atomic in the event loop; readers take the snapshot reference and render it. Across agents, exchange typed arrays over `postMessage`/transferables, or use `SharedArrayBuffer` with `Atomics` - object graphs cannot be swapped atomically between threads.
pitfalls: `Readonly<T>` and `readonly` are erased at runtime and shallow: nested objects stay mutable, and a cast (`next as Frame`) reintroduces the write-after-publish bug.
Object spread copies one level - arrays and nested objects remain shared with the previous frame, so an 'immutable update' can mutate published state.
Types do not exist at runtime: sending a frame to a worker re-creates plain objects and the readonly guarantee is not carried over.

variants.name: Typed OffscreenCanvas back buffer presented as ImageBitmap
variants.implementation_notes: The rendering realization is the browser mechanism with typed handles: render the frame into an `OffscreenCanvas` with an `OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`, then present it with `transferToImageBitmap()` into an `ImageBitmapRenderingContext` obtained from the visible canvas. Keeping presentation separate from drawing means the visible surface only ever receives complete frames, and the drawing step can be typed against a narrow interface (for example a function taking the frame snapshot and the back-buffer context), which also lets tests substitute a stub renderer.
pitfalls: `getContext` can return null and the context types differ; a non-null assertion hides a real failure when the canvas already has another context type.
`transferToImageBitmap()` detaches the offscreen surface - reallocate or alternate two OffscreenCanvases between frames.
DOM typings vary with the `lib` setting in tsconfig; `OffscreenCanvas`/`ImageBitmapRenderingContext` need a recent target.
